title: Universally contractible free deletion complex of a pointed condensed set
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on a small coherent site of profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Work in internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], with internal relative tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. Write $A[X]$ for the free internal module on a condensed set $X$, with its canonical generalized generators $[x]$, as in [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-adjunction]. Let $X$ be a condensed set equipped with a global point $e:1\to X$. For $n\geq0$ put $Q_n=A[X^{n+1}]$. Let $d_0=\epsilon:Q_0\to A$ send $[x]$ to $1$, and for $n\geq1$ let $d_n:Q_n\to Q_{n-1}$ be the alternating linearized deletion map
$$d_n[x_0,\ldots,x_n]=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^i[x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,x_n].$$
These are internal-module morphisms and $d_0d_1=0$, $d_nd_{n+1}=0$ for $n\geq1$. The actual maps
$$h_{-1}:A\to Q_0,\quad a\mapsto a[e],\qquad h_n:Q_n\to Q_{n+1},\quad [x_0,\ldots,x_n]\mapsto[e,x_0,\ldots,x_n]$$
are natural in pointed condensed sets and satisfy
$$\epsilon h_{-1}=\operatorname{id}_A,\qquad d_1h_0+h_{-1}\epsilon=\operatorname{id}_{Q_0},\qquad d_{n+1}h_n+h_{n-1}d_n=\operatorname{id}_{Q_n}\quad(n\geq1).$$
The augmented complex $\cdots\to Q_1\to Q_0\to A\to0$ is exact, meaning equality of the image and kernel subobjects and epimorphic augmentation. For every internal $A$-module $T$, after the unit identification $A\otimes_A T\cong T$, the maps $h_n\otimes\operatorname{id}_T$ and $h_{-1}\otimes\operatorname{id}_T$ satisfy the same contracting identities for the tensored complex. This augmented tensored complex is exact, with split epimorphic augmentation to $T$. Neither flatness of $T$ nor a group structure on $X$ is assumed; no equivariance of the contracting maps is asserted.

proof.text: Use the fixed free-linearization comparison of [lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor]. Define augmentation as the free map to the cartesian tensor unit followed by its normalized unit isomorphism to the regular module. Define its section by the inverse isomorphism and the free pointed singleton tuple. The comparison gives augmentation, insertion and deletion formulas on generalized generators. The section formula follows by linearity from the unit-generator formula, since the evaluated terminal sheaf has a unique section. All chosen comparison isomorphisms are normalized by the fixed free adjunction [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-adjunction].

proof.text: Prove the double-deletion identity by product extensionality and Fin.succAbove_succAbove_succAbove_predAbove. Expand the composite of alternating sums. Partition pairs (i,j) according to j≤i and pair (i,j) with (j,i+1) in the complement; the identical composite free maps have opposite coefficients. This is the finite-sum bijection argument of Mathlib AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComplex.d_squared. At augmentation the two maps to the cartesian tensor unit coincide and their coefficients are 1 and -1.

proof.text: Product extensionality shows insertion followed by deletion zero is the identity, and insertion followed by deletion i+1 is deletion i followed by insertion. Apply the free functor, split the alternating sum into its zero and successor parts, and cancel to obtain the positive contracting identities. In degree zero the remaining singleton is the pointed tuple, so the augmentation-section term cancels it. The augmentation after its section is the identity because the cartesian tensor unit is terminal and the normalized unit maps are inverse.

proof.text: Check coordinatewise that powers of a map commute with deletion, and that a pointed map commutes with insertion and the singleton tuple. Apply functoriality of the free functor and distribute composition over finite sums to prove boundary and insertion naturality. Uniqueness of maps to the cartesian tensor unit proves augmentation naturality; the pointed equation proves section naturality.

proof.text: Transfer abelianness through [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], using [lem-pur-ringed-site-module-category-abelian]. In an abelian category a short complex f,g is exact iff kernel.ι g followed by cokernel.π f vanishes. Compose h f + g k = id with these two maps: the f term vanishes by the cokernel equation, and the g term by the kernel equation. This proves exactness in zero and every positive degree. The specified augmentation section makes augmentation split epic.

proof.text: Use the proved MonoidalPreadditive instance for the internal relative tensor of [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor], which is implemented upstream in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.ModuleObjects.Monoidal. Apply the additive functor tensorRight T to the complex and contracting identities. At augmentation conjugate by the left unitor; its inverse cancels the unitor in the degree-zero contraction and in the augmentation-section composite. This yields exactly the specified tensored maps and identities without using flatness or preservation of kernels.

proof.text: Apply the same kernel-cokernel exactness argument from step 5 to the tensored complex and contracting identities. The specified tensored section is a section of the tensored augmentation and hence proves it epic. This uses only additivity of tensor and the point, without flatness of the coefficients or a group law on the condensed set.
